q: 1. Cross drainage works are not required when the canal is completely .............
explain: A ridge canal follows the highest line of the land; since streams flow away from the ridge on both sides, the canal never crosses a natural drainage path.

q: 2. Which one of the following is different from the rest .............
explain: Shotcrete, cement concrete, and precast concrete are all cement-based rigid linings. Asphaltic lining uses bitumen and is considered a flexible or different material category.

q: 3. Kennedy's gauge outlet comes under the category of .............
explain: Semi-modules (or flexible modules) are outlets where the discharge depends only on the water level in the supply canal and is independent of the field channel level.

q: 4. In siphon aqueduct the depth of d/s cut-off below high flood level is taken as .............
explain: To ensure stability against scouring of the river bed, the downstream cut-off is typically taken to a depth of $1.5R$ (where R is the Lacey's scour depth).

q: 5. The top of the weir or spillway is called .............
explain: The crest is the highest part of the overflow section of a dam, weir, or spillway.

q: 6. If the water table is nearer to the ground surface, an unlined irrigation canal may become useless because .............
explain: A high water table leads to excessive seepage, which triggers waterlogging in the command area (ayacut). This creates stagnant water conditions conducive to mosquito breeding and disease.

q: 7. Lacey's regime condition will be realized, if .............
options: silt grade in the channel is variable
channel flows in unlimited, incoherent alluvium of the same character as that of transported material
discharge in the channel is variable
silt charge in the channel is variable
explain: True regime is an ideal state where the channel bed and banks are made of the same material that the river is transporting, allowing the channel to adjust its dimensions freely.

q: 8. The main reason for the silting up of a canal is .............
explain: Silting occurs if the velocity is too low (inadequate slope), if the channel shape isn't balanced for the silt load, or if the head regulator fails to exclude heavy silt at the intake.

q: 9. When a canal and natural drain approach each other at a same elevation, the cross drainage work provided is .............
explain: A level crossing is used when the bed levels of the canal and the drain are nearly the same. The waters are allowed to mix and are then regulated through gates.

q: 10. An excavation filled with impervious material to reduce seepage is called
explain: Both cut-off trenches and key trenches are used in dam construction to intercept seepage through pervious foundations by filling a trench with impervious clay or concrete.

q: 11. The siphon well drop is ideal for
explain: Siphon well drops (or cylinder falls) are economical and efficient specifically for small discharges coupled with high drop heights.

q: 12. Fluming of a canal in the cross-drainage work will
options: reduce the cost of cross drainage work
enable the canal to draw water from drain
explain: Fluming involves contracting the canal width at a structure to reduce the length of the barrel/bridge, thereby saving construction costs.

q: 13. The slope of the sides of a Cippoletti weir is
explain: A Cippoletti weir is a trapezoidal weir with side slopes of 1 horizontal to 4 vertical, designed to compensate for end contractions.

q: 14. The bed of the canal is lowered in the case of
explain: In a canal siphon (also known as a barrel siphon), the canal is taken below the drainage bed by depressing its bed level to allow the water to flow under pressure.

q: 15. Inundation canals draw their supplies from rivers whenever there is
explain: Inundation canals do not have a headwork (weir/barrage) and only receive water when the river level rises during floods.

q: 16. The free board in a channel is governed by the
explain: Freeboard is the safety margin between the full supply level and the top of the bank to prevent overtopping.

q: 17. In case of small channels, the borrow pits should start from a distance not less than ............. from the toe of the embankment.
explain: A safe distance (minimum 5m) is maintained to prevent the borrow pit from undermining the stability of the canal embankment.

q: 18. For the repairing of an old but sound concrete lining, the lining preferred is
explain: Shotcrete (pneumatically applied mortar) is ideal for repairing cracks or resurfacing existing concrete structures.

q: 19. According to Kennedy, the silt transporting power of a channel is proportional to
explain: Kennedy derived that the silt carrying capacity of a channel varies with the 2.5 (or 5/2) power of its velocity.

q: 20. According to Lacey, a channel is said to be in regime, if
options: it flows in incoherent unlimited alluvium of the same character as that transported material
the silt grade and the silt charge are constant
explain: Lacey's 'True Regime' conditions require constant discharge, constant silt properties, and flow through an unlimited alluvial bed.

q: 21. A fall, which maintains the depth is a
explain: A trapezoidal notch fall is designed so that the depth-discharge relationship of the fall matches the canal itself, maintaining constant depth.

q: 22. A parabolic glacis type fall is commonly known as
explain: The Montague fall utilizes a parabolic glacis to efficiently guide water into the cistern and promote energy dissipation.

q: 23. When the water is thrown into a well over a crest from where it escapes near its bottom, the type of fall is called
explain: A cylinder fall (well fall) uses a vertical shaft to drop water, making it suitable for very large drops and small discharges.

q: 24. For the pipe outlet to be proportional, the outlet is set at .......... the depth below the water surface.
explain: For a pipe outlet to achieve proportionality, the depth of its center below the water surface should be roughly 0.3 times the depth of the channel.

q: 25. The slope of a canal, for a discharge of 300 cumec, should be .............
explain: For large discharges like 300 cumecs, the canal slope is generally flatter; 1 in 6000 is a standard design value for such high-capacity main canals.

q: 26. A solid construction put across the river to raise its water level and divert the water into the canal is known as .............
explain: A weir is a low-height solid obstruction used to raise the water level. While a barrage also does this, the primary definition for a solid construction of this nature is a weir.

q: 27. The loss of head in the hydraulic jump is given by .............
explain: The energy loss ($H_L$) in a hydraulic jump in a rectangular channel is mathematically expressed as $(D_2 - D_1)^3 / (4 D_1 D_2)$.

q: 28. The bed of a canal is lowered in case of .............
explain: In a canal siphon, the canal bed is depressed or lowered below its normal grade to pass under the drainage/obstruction.

q: 29. According to Lacey, in regime conditions .............
options: silt is kept in suspension by vertical components of eddies
entire cross-section of the channel is generated at all points by the forces normal to the wetted perimeter
explain: Unlike Kennedy (who only considered vertical eddies from the bed), Lacey stated that eddies are generated from the entire wetted perimeter.

q: 30. The main cause of silting up a channel, is .............
explain: Silting occurs when the velocity is too low to keep sediment in suspension, caused by poor design, low slopes, or excessive silt entry at the head.

q: 31. F.S.L. of a canal at its head with respect to parent channel is kept .............
explain: The Full Supply Level (FSL) of the taking-off canal is usually kept about 15 cm lower than the parent canal to ensure draw-off even when the parent canal is not at full supply.

q: 32. If the straight sides of a triangular section of a lined canal with circular bottom of radius D, make an angle θ with horizontal, the hydraulic mean depth is .............
explain: For a triangular section with a rounded bottom, the hydraulic mean depth (Area/Perimeter) simplifies to R/2 (or D/2 if D is the radius).

q: 33. In concrete canal the approximate permissible velocity of water should not exceed .............
explain: Concrete lining can withstand higher velocities without erosion; the typical upper limit to prevent damage is around 2 to 2.5 m/sec.

q: 34. For the design of major hydraulic structures on the canals, the method generally preferred is based on .............
explain: Khosla's method is the modern standard because it accounts for the actual flow net and the influence of various floor components independently.

q: 35. To hold hydraulic jumps, baffle walls are provided in .............
explain: The English (or Baffle) fall uses a specific wall on the floor to stabilize the hydraulic jump and dissipate energy.

q: 36. Bed bars in a canal are provided .............
options: to watch the general behavior of canal
explain: Bed bars are masonry or concrete strips built across the canal bed at intervals to serve as permanent benchmarks for monitoring siltation or scour.
